description.narrative:
Considering these needs in the specific locations targeted, DPNA and Plan's response will prioritise WASH, with drinking water and hygiene kits, including Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM) supplies. With the onset of winter, NFIs will be distributed to provide winterisation support for those most in need. To address the immediate nutritional needs of displaced families, food kits and Ready-to-Eat (RTE) meals will be distributed. Given the severe psychological toll and protection risks, strong protection mainstreaming will be put in place.
The action is designed with the core objective of providing lifesaving assistance to the most affected people and meet critical needs identified, while adhering to sectoral, international and local standards (including FSL, WASH and basic assistance national sector recommendations in addition to the CHS).

Due to the escalation of violent conflict in the Middle East, Lebanon is currently facing a major acute crisis characterised by sudden, large-scale displacement. Based on the guidelines of the recommendation paper developed by DRA members and on Plan International and DPNA’s own assessments, the action initially targeted Chouf and Aley in Mt. Lebanon and Saida in the South governorate. These locations were chosen due to the fact that they hosted a large number of IDPs and because of the situation in the collective shelters. After the ceasefire in November 2024, many displaced people returned to their hometowns. In line with recommendations from the sector working group, activities are now shifted to the Southern Suburbs and Tyre being priority areas where Plan International and DPNA can better address the needs of displaced populations.

Plan and DPNA focus on targeting vulnerable groups identified as most in need within the conflict-affected population, ensuring inclusivity and prioritising those disproportionately impacted by the crisis. Beneficiary identification is conducted in close collaboration with municipalities and through referrals from the Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) teams, aligning with sector-specific criteria to ensure effective and transparent targeting.

Plan will combine direct operations with a collaboration with our local partner DPNA, who will have a leading role and was fully involved in the design. Plan will lead the direct implementation in the Southern Suburbs (FSL/WASH/NFIs), leveraging its strong operational presence, while DPNA will lead in Tyre (FSL/WASH) based on their deep community ties and a strong understanding of the local context.
DPNA was actively involved through the needs assessments and the identification of critical gaps as well as full ownership of the design of activities in Tyre. DPNA is supported by Plan through capacity building, technical guidance, logistical support, and resource sharing.
The JR consortium under the lead of War Child has coordinated extensively to prevent overlap and create synergies wherever possible.

SUMMARY Lebanon is currently facing a major acute crisis characterised by sudden, large-scale displacement. Together with local partner Development for People and Nature Association (DPNA), Plan International is providing a humanitarian response that focuses on the provision of food security, WASH and shelter items, with a strong protection mainstreaming element. Initially, the intervention was designed to target crisis-affected people in collective shelters in Chouf and Aley districts in Mt. Lebanon, and Saida in the South governorate. After the ceasefire of November 2024, the activities were shifted to target the most vulnerable people in Tyre and the Southern Suburbs. The response is funded by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs through the Dutch Relief Alliance (DRA), with Plan International and DPNA being part of a larger consortium that operates through this Acute Crisis Joint Response.

The action is designed with the core objective of providing basic assistance to IDPs and other vulnerable groups in the Southern Suburbs and Tyre to meet the urgent needs identified, while adhering to sectoral, international and local standards (including FSL, WASH and Basic assistance national sector recommendations in addition to the CHS).
The activities focus on WASH, food security, winterisation and protection mainstreaming. Plan and DPNA adopt a needs-based approach, starting with the provision of critical WASH services to ensure access to safe drinking water and hygiene supplies, including MHM kits. This is particularly crucial in substandard living conditions, where IDPs lack basic sanitation and hygiene facilities. The provision of winterisation NFIs, such as blankets, is planned to mitigate the harsh impacts of winter on vulnerable families. Simultaneously, the distribution of food kits, including Ready-to-Eat (RTE) meals in shelters that lack kitchens, will address immediate nutritional needs.
The action is designed in close coordination with local and national actors, leveraging the expertise and reach of local partners and communities. Plan works alongside JR members, local municipalities, and relevant authorities to ensure complementarity with ongoing efforts. Plan’s emergency response plan for the current situation was in place several months in advance and is thus being implemented since the very start of the latest escalation, building on Plan’s Ready to Respond approach. Emergency assistance is ongoing and the acute DRA funding will allow an immediate scale-up using Plan/DPNA’s existing infrastructure, procurement processes, and established contracts with suppliers and vendors (for items such as hygiene kits, blankets, and food kits).

comment.narrative: The JR had to be modified due to the ceasefire, which in the case of Plan and DPNA led to a location change. Planned distribution was paused to conduct further assessments by the sector and DRR teams, ensuring that resources are allocated effectively and reach those most in need. With a clearer understanding of the situation and in close coordination with the municipalities and DRR, Plan and DPNA have started distribution mid-January in the newly designated areas, ensuring an optimised and needs-driven response.
